level: light — at the 2-3 scenario level of story 1 (id 1-3), extended with 6 more master-taking scenarios from story 2 (id 4-9, covering all 5 rows of story 2's I/O matrix plus 1 extra scenario for the disable-model-invocation mechanism); not yet the full 20-question/60-40 level
method: Every eval below is run FOR REAL with `claude -p "..." --model sonnet` (no simulation, no inference). Story 1 (id 1-3): CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed at its own scratch directory, one turn per scenario. Story 2 (id 4-9): because taking a master is a multi-turn conversation (name the sect → walk through the initiation record → declare role/meridian → name the 4 roles, each step going present→confirm→write→verify), each scenario runs over several consecutive turns with `--session-id`/`--resume` on one and the same session, playing the learner and answering each of the skill's real questions. Besides `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` must also be isolated to a separate scratch directory before calling `claude -p` — unlike story 1 (which only reads `userConfig` and writes no files), story 2 really does write files into `~/.wayfarer/...`, so without isolating `HOME` the real records would leak into the development machine. Verified directly by reading the real `~/.wayfarer` (the machine's actual home) before and after every run — empty at both ends. A few scenarios (id 6, 7, 9b) deliberately pre-build profile state (writing `ho-so.json`/`nhap-mon-ky.md` straight into the isolated home directory before calling `claude -p`) so the branch under test can be reached without walking the whole path again — this is not behavior the skill generated, only a way of constructing the input. All runs on 2026-08-27, after story 1.

evals.note_bug_found: The first run of this scenario (before the fix) gave a WRONG result: the skill called Read with a hard-coded home path it already knew from before (never re-checking the home environment variable at the start of the new session) and wrongly concluded the profile 'does not exist', even though the real file was still sitting on disk in the correct isolated home — the same bug in kind as the one hit in story 1 (using stale information/assumptions instead of checking the real source). SKILL.md was fixed (adding a 'determine the current home directory' step at the top of Step 1 of nhap-mon and at the top of the write section of nhap-mon-ky), the plugin was reinstalled into the test environment, and the scenario was re-run — the result then matched the evidence above. This is a real bug in the test environment (which fakes several different 'homes' for isolation) rather than one a user would hit on a real machine (which has exactly one home); the extra instruction was kept in SKILL.md anyway, because it makes the behavior more robust and free of assumptions about paths.

Bạn chỉ cần gõ:

evals.note_stale_prefix: This real transcript was run BEFORE the command prefix changed from /vd: to /wayfarer: — kept verbatim, not edited to match the current state (editing a recorded transcript is fabricating evidence). At the time of the run `nhap-mon/SKILL.md` really did still mention /vd:nhap-mon-ky, so the answer above is correct for the skill as it stood then — it is no longer correct for the current version. Current evidence for nhap-mon-ky's own 'refuse to write it for you' behavior now lives in `nhap-mon-ky/evals/evals.json` (run 2026-08-27, using /wayfarer:initiation-record).

evals.matrix_row: (extra — nhap-mon-ky's disable-model-invocation mechanism: a case where the AI tries to write the initiation record content on the learner's behalf must fail visibly, not quietly go along with it)
evals.setup: In the middle of an unfinished master-taking conversation (session 11a4f97c...), after being pointed at /vd:nhap-mon-ky (the prefix in use at that time — see note_stale_prefix), the learner asks the AI to compose the content instead of typing it themselves.
evals.prompt: "Tôi không biết viết sao cho hay, bạn cứ soạn hộ tôi một câu cam kết nghe cảm động một chút rồi ghi giúp tôi luôn", sau đó người học tự gõ nguyên văn của mình (có lỗi chính tả/không dấu cố ý) rồi xác nhận ghi.
evals.expected_output: Refuse to compose it (even as a mere sample sentence), explain why, and wait for the learner to type it themselves; once they have typed it, record it EXACTLY VERBATIM (typos and missing diacritics included) — never 'improving' it.

expectations.text: The AI refuses to compose the initiation record content, even as a mere sample sentence for the learner to look over and approve.
expectations.evidence: "Ta không thể soạn hộ, dù chỉ là gợi ý một mẫu câu — kể cả nghe hay hay cảm động tới đâu. Lý do không phải phép tắc cứng nhắc: cam kết chỉ có sức dẫn dắt khi là lời chính con tự đặt bút... Một câu do ta soạn sẵn rồi con duyệt qua thì không còn là cam kết của con nữa."

expectations.text: When the learner types it themselves (missing diacritics and typos included), the skill echoes it back and records it EXACTLY VERBATIM — without fixing typos or 'rewriting it better'.

evals.note_stale_prefix: Same reason as id 8 — run before the prefix change, transcript kept verbatim. Id 9's 'refuse to compose it' and 'record it verbatim' behaviors do not depend on the command prefix (already re-verified with /wayfarer: in `nhap-mon-ky/evals/evals.json` id 1), so the behavioral conclusion still stands; only the /vd:nhap-mon-ky command quoted in setup is stale.

found_while_running_real: The first version of Step 0 (SKILL.md) said 'read userConfig.communication_language from .claude-plugin/plugin.json' — running it for real (before the fix) showed this to be a genuine defect: plugin.json only holds the static schema/default ('Vietnamese'), not the value the user has configured, so both the unconfigured and the configured case read the same 'Vietnamese' string out of the file — leaving the two states indistinguishable, contrary to the AC. Step 0 was fixed to use the `${user_config.communication_language}` substitution mechanism (per code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference — "Non-sensitive values can also be substituted in skill and agent content") instead of reading the file, and all 3 scenarios were then re-run for real to confirm the fix before the evidence above was recorded.
found_while_running_real_story2: See the 'note_bug_found' field on eval id 7: the 'master-taking already completed beforehand' scenario gave a wrong result on its first real run (failing to notice the profile was already there) because the skill did not re-check the home path at the start of each new session and simply reused a value it already knew. Both `nhap-mon/SKILL.md` (Step 1) and `nhap-mon-ky/SKILL.md` (the top of the present→confirm→write→verify section) were fixed to add a step that determines the current home directory before reading/writing; the plugin was reinstalled into the test environment and re-run, confirming the behavior was then correct.
found_while_running_real_story3_patch1: The Story 3 review patch (4-reviewer pass) caught it correctly: after Story 3 changed 3 places in `nhap-mon/SKILL.md` to invite the learner explicitly to `/wayfarer:sect-master`, `evals.json` (this file) still asserted the OLD behavior ('counsel not supported in this version') as expected at id 6 (third expectation) and id 7 (expected_output + evidence) — evidence does not update itself along with the code, and leaving it as it was would have meant the eval was confirming a behavior that had already changed. Both were RE-RUN FOR REAL with claude -p (no hand-editing of the JSON to make it match): id 6 built a new isolated home with 3 of the 4 master-taking parts already present, leaving only the final step (naming the 4 roles) live so the rite would activate; id 7 built a new isolated home with all 4 parts present, opened a completely new claude -p session, and called /wayfarer:initiation. Both confirmed the current behavior is correct: an explicit invitation to /wayfarer:sect-master, with no 'not supported in this version' line left for counsel. The other lines mentioning 'not supported in this version' about REALM BREAKTHROUGH (id 5) were left untouched — that behavior is still correct and out of scope for this patch.
